1ro2iz2: Amina started volunteering at a community library and during the first week wrote down several questions. She didn't understand why some people went straight into the meeting room and others waited by the front desk. At first she thought there was a rule nobody had explained to her. Later she discovered that it depended on the activity: groups with a reservation could go in, while new visitors had to ask where each inquiry was handled.
7op4ln: The coordinator decided to prepare a short guide with the team. They avoided phrases like «aquí todo el mundo sabe» and described concrete situations. Books are lent for two weeks; silence is requested in the small room; talking is allowed in the workshops. The guide also clarifies that the main door is closed during the break, although the building stays open through the side entrance. That is an important difference for someone arriving for the first time.
1tzfnye: The volunteers help one another during setup. Each person organizes themselves before opening, but when a doubt comes up, a common answer is sought so as not to give contradictory instructions.
1x34kkr: Amina added a recommendation: when someone doesn't understand an instruction, it's better to rephrase it than to automatically speak louder. An unfamiliar word or a fast pace doesn't mean lack of attention. The library began to use examples and to point out the spaces while explaining. The new guide didn't claim to represent the customs of a whole city. It recorded agreements from one specific place and reminded people that anyone could ask about their meaning or propose an improvement.
